title: Ariana Grande Announces Career Hiatus to Focus on Mental Health and Healing
text:
Pop superstar Ariana Grande bids farewell to the stage and announces a break from the public eye to recover from PTSD and the pressures of fame.
Ariana Grande, a towering figure in 21st-century pop music, has reached a poignant crossroads in her career. At 33 years old, the singer has achieved a level of success that few can fathom, selling over 90 million records and garnering numerous Grammy Awards and Guinness World Records.
Her transition from a child star on Nickelodeon to a critically acclaimed actress, including an Oscar-nominated role, marks a versatile artistic journey. However, this glittering exterior has often masked a profound internal struggle. On a recent Tuesday, Grande emotionally bid farewell to the spotlight during the final performance of her Eternal Sunshine tour at the O2 Arena in London.
The atmosphere was heavy with emotion as fans realized this would be the last time they would see her perform for the foreseeable future. Her management team confirmed that the star is taking a necessary hiatus from public-facing work to escape the relentless and ongoing scrutiny of the public eye. The singer has been remarkably open about the psychological toll that stardom and tragedy have taken on her.
Her journey toward healing has been fraught with challenges, primarily rooted in two catastrophic events. In 2017, the world watched as a suicide bomber targeted her concert in Manchester, leaving 22 people dead and over a thousand injured. The aftermath left Grande with a diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder, which manifested not only as emotional distress but also as debilitating physical symptoms.
She described experiencing sudden dizzy spells and a suffocating feeling of being unable to breathe, often striking her without warning even during moments of happiness. To combat these effects, she turned to professional therapy and the creative process. Her album Sweetener served as a lifeline, allowing her to channel her grief, depression, and anxiety into melodies. She has noted that treating her mental health with the same seriousness as her career was essential for her survival during those dark times.
Adding to her burden, shortly after the release of Sweetener, Grande faced another devastating blow when her former partner passed away due to an accidental overdose. The grief from this loss was overwhelming, prompting her to create the album Thank U Next in a mere two weeks. This project was born out of a desperate need for emotional release rather than commercial strategy.
Despite the hesitations of her record label, who were reluctant to pivot so quickly from her previous work, Grande insisted on following her intuition for the sake of her own soul. This period of vulnerability allowed her to connect with millions of fans who shared similar pains, breaking the polished facade of a pop idol to reveal a human being in pain.
By choosing honesty over perfection, she found a path toward healing and a way to feel heard and safe. Despite these strides in recovery, the fragility of mental health remains a constant battle. The pressures of being in the spotlight since childhood, coupled with the recurring triggers of fame, have periodically set her back.
Most recently, an incident at the Wicked premiere in Singapore, where an overzealous fan jumped a barrier and grabbed her, served as a stark reminder of the volatility of her public existence. This event, combined with the cumulative exhaustion of a decade of high-intensity performance and media intrusion, has led to the decision to step away.
By prioritizing her wellbeing over her professional obligations, Ariana Grande is attempting to reclaim her peace and finalize a healing journey that began years ago. This hiatus represents a courageous act of self-preservation, ensuring that the artist can eventually return to her craft with a renewed sense of stability and strength
